title: Rectify inconsistent aggregate credits from request-coalescing across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
Multiple customers (Hosted + Dedicated + Private) reported month-to-date invoice deltas where the sum of per-session token attributions did not match the ledger-aggregated credit totals. Root cause (initial hypothesis): the request-coalescing layer (introduced in runtime-1.23 to reduce duplicate upstreams for near-identical prompt bundles) is collapsing concurrent identical requests across replicas but failing to reconcile per-tenant attribution in the ledger emission path when coalescing spans multiple routing tiers (hosted -> dedicated fallback, or dedupe across private node groups). In certain timing windows we observed either double-emit or drop of the metering event for coalesced requests, depending on which replica finished first and which path acknowledged the request.

Reproduction steps (intermittent, race dependent):
1) Run 50 concurrent identical generation requests from a single tenant across two simultaneous routing tiers (hosted primary with dedicated fallback).
2) Force request coalescing by ensuring identical prompt + model + parameters and short TTL on KV cache.
3) Observe emitted metering events in the ingestion pipeline (kafka topic: metering.events) and compare per-request tokens vs ledger-aggregates produced by billing-rollup (job: billing-rollup-hourly).

Observed behavior:
- In ~1.2% of runs a coalesced request results in only the fallback replica emitting the metering event while the primary's emission path considers the request served and suppresses its emit -> ledger undercount for the tenant.
- In ~0.6% of runs both replicas emit (race where both ack) -> double-counted tokens and unexpected credit application.

Immediate mitigation applied (03/11):
- Short-term hotfix: toggled request-coalescing to conservative mode (coalesce only within a single routing tier) via feature flag FF_METERING_SAFE_COALESCE=false across Hosted and Dedicated. This stopped new customer-facing deltas while we investigate.
- Manual ledger backfill started for impacted customers with discrepant days (tracked in spreadsheet and support tickets).

Root cause analysis (work-in-progress):
- The coalescing coordinator relied on an in-memory leader election per-coalescing-key that did not account for cross-tier acknowledgements. The metering emission code path assumed idempotence based on local request-id, but the fallback flow introduced a different request-id and both paths can independently emit.
- Missing invariant: exactly-one-metering-event-per-finalized-response across the cluster (regardless of coalescing).

Proposed fix plan (4 sprints, staged):
1) Short patch (P0, 1 week): centralize metering emission to a single, deterministic emitter chosen by coalescing coordinator and propagate a canonical meter_id in the routed response. Add zookeeper-style ephemeral lease keyed by coalesce-key so only lease-holder emits. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8842)
2) Hardening (P1, 2 weeks): add strong end-to-end tests that simulate cross-tier coalescing, add property-based tests for exactly-one emission, and instrument metrics for emit_counts_per_request_id.
3) Rollout & verification (2 weeks): canary across 5% of traffic in Hosted, mirrored Dedicated cluster with opt-in customers, and private customer opt-in package.
4) Post-rollback/backfill plan: automated reconciliation job to detect mismatched aggregates and emit correction entries with audit trail.

Rollout & verification steps:
- Feature gated with FF_METERING_SAFE_COALESCE; new deterministic emitter behind FF_METERING_SINGLE_EMITTER.
- Monitor metrics: metering.emit_count_per_request, metering.duplicate_emits, billing.ledger_discrepancy_rate.
- Add Grafana dashboard panel: "Metering Emissions by Request Key" and alert if duplicate_emits > 0.1% for 15m.

Customer communication:
- Drafted customer-facing note for impacted tenants explaining root cause, mitigation, and remediation timeline (Confluence: https://confluence.redwoodinc.com/display/BILL/Coalesce-Metering-Incident).
- Support owners assigned to contact top 10 impacted customers with proposed ledger backfills and credit adjustments.

Acceptance criteria:
- Deploy patch removing duplicate/dropped metering events in canary with zero escalation for 48h.
- Billing-rollup reconciliation runs produce <=0.01% ledger deltas vs golden baseline on canary traffic.
- Post-deploy backfill applied and validated for all previously impacted days.

2026-03-12 Priya Nair (SRE): Observed two failure modes in demo cluster. Captured trace IDs and Sentry group: https://sentry.redwoodinc.com/organizations/redwood/issues/COALESCE-EMIT-122. Added ephemeral lease prototype to try to enforce single emitter.

2026-03-12 Engineering review: Reviewed initial PR 8842. Request from review: ensure emitter lease survives router failover and include telemetry for lease-acquire/lease-lost. Assigned to Lucas for follow-up.

2026-03-13 QA Lucas Rivera: End-to-end smoke tests added to CI job billing-e2e. Local stress reproduced duplicate emit in 7/1000 runs; patched coordinator to include canonical meter_id propagation. Preparing canary tomorrow.
